headline: The real house, rebuilt room by room until a critic stops telling them apart
lede: Every room of this house is being rebuilt as procedural 3D geometry inside the live Home Assistant app, then screenshotted from the same spot the reference photo was taken. A separate critic with fresh context puts the two side by side, blind, and says which is which. If ours is obvious, it goes back to the builder. The bar for the overall look is The Sims 4's dollhouse build view; the bar for each room is the photograph of that actual room.
stamp: round 2 · geometry re-traced house-wide · exterior finished
hero_label: The exterior, finished against the photograph: light-grey architectural roof, near-black front door, river-rock foundation beds with boxwood and perennials, the SUV in the driveway, bin, porch planters and path lights.

rooms.name: Master Bedroom
rooms.note: Round 3 rebuilt from measurement, not guesswork. The bed was proved to be a QUEEN, not a king, by three independent photo anchors — which also explained why the wall art 'looked huge': the ruler was wrong, not the canvas. The 15 ft north wall is now solved as one budget (dresser, window, bed, nightstand) so the long-standing collision between the dresser, the window and the headboard is gone. Vault ridge moved off-centre to sit over the bed, matching the photo's asymmetric gable. Builder also found and fixed a real bug in the screenshot harness: the camera pose never waited for its target to converge, so every earlier comparison was framed slightly off. — Footprint has since been re-traced, so this room's furniture needs re-placing before it can be judged again.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.note: Round 2 in progress: re-placing every piece into the re-traced footprint and fixing the critic's list. The fake internal wall and its 190 sq ft of dead floor are gone with the re-trace.

rooms.name: Living Room
rooms.note: Round 2 in progress: re-placing every piece into the re-traced footprint and fixing the critic's list. The north wall lost 10 ft, so what round 1 packed onto it has to be re-derived from the photos.

rooms.name: Dining
rooms.note: 15 pieces including a real tray ceiling with a medallion, chair rail and picture-frame wainscot, eight parsons chairs, a black six-arm chandelier, and blinds at 44 percent with lawn and porch rail visible through the gap. Orientation was derived rather than assumed by cross-referencing all four photos against the house layout. — Footprint has since been re-traced, so this room's furniture needs re-placing before it can be judged again.

rooms.name: Rios Room
rooms.note: Critic: FAIL. Biggest gap is the windows — built 6.15 ft tall where the photo measures about 4.8 ft, so they read as French doors, which crushes the apparent ceiling height and makes the whole room look oversized. The rubber plant intersects the window, the birdcage and the north wall. Nothing casts a contact shadow. — Footprint has since been re-traced, so this room's furniture needs re-placing before it can be judged again.
